instruction: Open your web browser and navigate to the downloads page to check your download history.

metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome's downloads page (chrome://downloads/). Uses existing evaluator functions - is_expected_active_tab_approximate metric and active_url_from_accessTree getter. No new functions needed. Similar difficulty to original task (simple navigation).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: active_url_from_accessTree extracts the URL from Chrome's address bar via accessibility tree, which is the right approach for verifying navigation
Metric logic is correct: is_expected_active_tab_approximate compares URLs while ignoring query parameters, appropriate for URL matching
Complete coverage: Evaluator checks if active tab URL is chrome://downloads/, which fully verifies the instruction requirement to navigate to downloads management page
Data flow is semantically correct: getter returns URL string, metric compares URL against expected chrome://downloads/
Expected value is correct: chrome://downloads/ is the actual Chrome internal URL for downloads management page
No postconfig needed: accessibility tree reflects current browser state, persistent after task completion
Edge cases handled: metric handles both string URLs and dict objects, strips query parameters for flexible matching, returns 0 if no tab info found
